entry.title: Seamless Mobile-to-Web Single Sign-On with the Joule Work mobile app
entry.content:
With version 3.0, Joule Work mobile app (formerly known as SAP Mobile Start) introduces a feature that many customers have been asking for: seamless Single Sign-On when opening web applications in the in-app browser. In this post I want to explain the problem this feature solves, how it works conceptually, and what administrators need to configure to enable it.

The Problem: Two Sessions, One App Experience

Joule Work mobile app (formerly known as SAP Mobile Start), when connected to SAP Build Work Zone, is the native mobile entry point for the Intelligent Enterprise. From a single app, users can access native features like widgets, push notifications, and smartwatch complications, but also launch web applications directly from the app – for example SAP Fiori apps from SAP S/4HANA, collaborative Workspaces in SAP Build Work Zone, advanced edition, custom extensions build on the SAP Business Technology Platform, and more.

When a user taps on a tile that opens a web application, the Joule Work mobile app instantiates the in-app browser provided by the mobile operating system – iOS or Android. This is a technical context switch: the native application session, which is managed by SAP Mobile Services and backed by SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication, is logically separated from the browser sessions of web applications, for example SAP S/4HANA Public Cloud Edition.

As a result, the in-app browser may not have a valid session for the target web application when launched. The user is redirected to the identity provider and prompted to log in again. This is particularly jarring because, from the user's perspective, they are just navigating within their app.

The Previous Recommendation – and Why It Was Not Ideal for all customers

Customers could avoid this by enabling the "Remember me" functionality of SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication. This feature creates a long-living session cookie in the browser, keeping users signed in across browser sessions for a configurable duration. A similar capability exists on many corporate identity providers (third-party IdPs) to which SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication may be configured delegating the actual authentication. Long-lived cookies on these providers effectively keep the user session alive in the in-app browser in the same manner.

However, this approach has a fundamental drawback: long-lived session cookies are not ideal and may not be wanted to be generically configured on the company's Identity Provider. Furthermore, "Remember me" only prolongs the time until a user is asked to sign-in again in the in-app browser – it is not fully getting rid of it.

Another alternative that some customers consider is password-less sign-in using client certificates. While this is a genuinely secure and, once set up, a convenient approach, it is not feasible for all customers and all users. Client certificates typically require an active Mobile Device Management (MDM) system to push certificates to managed devices – meaning unmanaged devices, common in bring your own device (BYOD) environments, are excluded. Beyond the deployment challenge, mobile operating systems restrict access to the system keychain for third-party apps, so not all in-app browser variants can reliably make use of client certificates. Other password-less options such as FIDO passkeys or biometric-based flows can require some form of manual user interaction during authentication, which breaks the seamless experience users expect when tapping a tile in the app.

The New Solution: Mobile-to-Web SSO

With version 3.0, Joule Work mobile app introduces a dedicated Mobile-to-Web Single Sign-On flow that bridges the native session and the in-app browser – securely, without requiring long-lived cookies. Here is how it works conceptually:

The mobile app already holds a valid session with SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication (in the context of SAP Build Work Zone, to which the app is connected to). The SAP Cloud Identity Services tenant generally serves as the trust anchor for both SAP Build Work Zone, the native app and other SAP and non-SAP solutions including web applications exposed to SAP Build Work Zone. This shared trust is what makes it possible to bridge the two worlds: because both the native app session and the target web applications are anchored in the same SAP Cloud Identity Services tenant, it can act as a secure intermediary, translating the native session into a web session in the in-app browser without requiring the user to authenticate again.

When the user opens a web application in the in-app browser, the app first exchanges its active native session for a short-lived, one-time use SSO token issued by SAP Cloud Identity Services. This token is valid for only a very short time and can only be used once by the mobile app for (re-)establishing a session in the in-app browser on the mobile device.

This is done by passing this one-time SSO token to SAP Cloud Identity Services within the browser context. The SAP Cloud Identity Services validates the token, maps it to the user's identity & native session, and establishes a regular web session – setting the standard browser session cookies. From there, the accessed target web application authenticates against SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication transparently via its standard SAML or OIDC flow reusing the established IAS session with no user interaction required.

The key properties of this approach:

  • Security-friendly: The SSO token is a one-time use token with a short validity. There are no long-lived session cookies involved on the identity provider side.
  • Admin-controlled: The feature can be controlled via a feature flag in SAP Mobile Services Admin Cockpit of the Joule Work mobile app. The administrator also defines exactly which web applications are trusted for this flow by configuring them in SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication.
  • Broadly compatible: The feature works with all in-app browser variants offered by Joule Work mobile app on iOS and Android. It also works with all web applications – SAP solutions as well as custom or third-party apps – as long as they share a common SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication tenant with the environment the mobile app is onboarded to.

Key Prerequisite: SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication as the Common Trust Anchor

For the Mobile-to-Web SSO flow to work, SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication must be the identity provider for both the native mobile application and all web applications that should benefit from seamless SSO. The trust is established and maintained through SAP Cloud Identity Services, making it the single common denominator across all participants.

It is important to clarify that SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication does not need to be your end users' primary authentication system. In many enterprise landscapes, SAP Cloud Identity Services acts as an identity proxy, delegating the actual authentication to a corporate identity provider such as Microsoft Entra ID or other identity providers. This is fully supported. The only requirement is that SAP Cloud Identity Services is the first common trust anchor in the chain – meaning all participating web applications are configured to trust it directly, even if it in turn proxies to a corporate IdP.

One configuration detail to be aware of in proxy setups: the "Forward All SSO Requests to Corporate IdP" setting in SAP Cloud Identity Services must not be enabled for the applications involved in the Mobile-to-Web SSO flow. When this setting is active, SAP Cloud Identity Services bypasses its own session handling and always redirects to the corporate IdP – which would cause the Mobile-to-Web SSO token to be ignored, and users would end up with a login prompt again. Beyond Mobile-to-Web SSO, enabling this setting can also cause issues in iFrame-based in-place app integration scenarios, as corporate identity providers frequently block iFraming to protect against clickjacking and similar attack vectors. For more information on this setting, see Forward All SSO Requests to Corporate IdP (SAP Help).

The trust for the Mobile-to-Web SSO flow is configured explicitly in SAP Cloud Identity Services. The administrator defines which web application entries in SAP Cloud Identity Services are allowed to participate in this flow – only applications that have been explicitly added to the trust configuration can benefit from it. In addition, SAP Cloud Identity Services validates the URL of the target web application against the allowed redirect URIs configured for the trusted application. This means a web application can only receive a seamless SSO session if its URL matches one of the permitted redirect URI patterns. Both aspects – the application trust list and the redirect URI validation – ensure that the administrator retains full control over which applications can be reached via this mechanism.

Please note: Customers with SAP Build Work Zone subscriptions created before March 2025 may not yet be using SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication directly. For these environments, it is necessary to explicitly switch the authentication mechanism. Subscriptions created after that date are automatically set up with SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication. Please refer to the SAP Help documentation for the migration steps: Switching to SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication.

Pro tip: As with other features that depend on shared sessions and cookies – such as the iFrame-based in-place integration of web applications – it is important that all components share a common super domain. We strongly recommend operating SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication and your SAP cloud solutions under the SAP Common Super Domain cloud.sap, while other domains work as well as long as they are aligned across the stack to prevent cross-domain restrictions. If you are not yet familiar with this topic, our earlier blog post explains the background and the configuration steps in detail: Demystifying the Common Super Domain for SAP Mobile Start.

Which Web Applications Are Covered Automatically?

When Joule Work mobile app is connected to SAP Build Work Zone, both share the same Application entry in SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication. This means that SAP Build Work Zone itself is automatically within the trust scope – no additional configuration is needed for it.

This automatic coverage includes for example:

  • SAP Build Work Zone, advanced edition Workspaces – collaborative workspace content embedded in the Work Zone experience
  • Custom extensions hosted on SAP BTP – applications built for example with the SAP Cloud Application Programming Model, deployed to the SAP BTP and served using the Approuter of SAP Build Work Zone. (For details on building such extensions, see Building Pro-Code Extensions for SAP Mobile Start)
  • SAP Fiori apps from SAP S/4HANA On-Premise or SAP S/4HANA Cloud Private Edition running through an SAP Cloud Connector using a Principal Propagation Destination – these are tunneled through the BTP subaccount and are therefore covered by the same Application entry

The key distinction is that automatic coverage applies to applications that are part of – or tunneled through – the SAP BTP subaccount and its corresponding SAP Cloud Identity Services Application. Applications that run on their own infrastructure and have their own independent trust relationship with SAP Cloud Identity Services are not automatically covered, regardless of whether they are launched in embedded ("in-place") mode or opened directly ("ex-place"). A prominent example is SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition: even when it is iFramed within the SAP Build Work Zone shell, it has its own Application entry in SAP Cloud Identity Services and must be explicitly added to the Native-Web Trust group.

For all such web applications – SAP solutions with their own IAS Application entry, third-party apps, or any app not part of the Work Zone BTP subaccount – administrators add them to the trust configuration in SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication as described in the setup steps below.

Administrator Setup

Step 1: Verify That IAS-Based Authentication Is Active

Before enabling the feature, confirm that SAP Build Work Zone is using SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication as its identity provider. If this is not yet the case, follow the migration steps referenced in the prerequisite section above.

Step 2: Enable the Feature Flag in SAP Mobile Services

In the SAP Mobile Services Admin Cockpit, navigate to the Client Settings. In the Feature Flags section, locate the entry named "MobiletoWebSingleSign-On" and activate it.

Screenshot showing the highlighted feature flag in the activated state in the Mobile Services Admin Cockpit.

For reference, the corresponding documentation can be found here: Single Sign-On for Web Apps – SAP Help

Step 3: Add Trusted Web Applications in SAP Cloud Identity Services

For web applications that are not automatically covered through the SAP Build Work Zone application (see the previous section), you can add them to the trust configuration:

  1. Sign in to the administration console for SAP Cloud Identity Services.
  2. Go to Applications & Resources → Applications.
  3. Select the application entry that corresponds to your SAP Build Work Zone instance.
  4. Go to the Trust tab, then navigate to Application APIs → Dependencies → Native-Web Trust.
  5. Click Add and select the application with which you want to establish trust.
  6. Save your selection.

Screenshot of SAP Cloud Identity Services to maintain Native-Web Trust Settings

Users opening applications from this trust list in the in-app browser will now benefit from the seamless Mobile-to-Web SSO flow.

Step 4: Verify the Redirect URIs of Trusted Applications

As described in the prerequisite section, SAP Cloud Identity Services validates the URL of the target web application against the allowed redirect URIs of the trusted application entry. For SAP-delivered solutions – such as SAP S/4HANA Cloud Public Edition – the redirect URIs are typically pre-configured correctly by SAP and no further action is needed.

However, for custom-built applications or third-party web apps that rely on the general SAP Business Technology Platform application entry in SAP Cloud Identity Services, you should verify that the application's URL is covered by the configured redirect URI patterns. If the URL does not match any permitted pattern, the Mobile-to-Web SSO flow will not complete successfully for that application.

You can review and adjust the redirect URIs in the SAP Cloud Identity Services administration console under the application's configuration. For the rules and wildcard syntax supported for redirect URIs, refer to the SAP Help documentation: Redirect URIs and Post Logout Redirect URI Rules (SAP Help).

Summary

With the Mobile-to-Web SSO feature, Joule Work mobile app version 3.0 closes the session gap between the native app context and the in-app browser – cleanly, securely, and with full administrator control.

Key takeaways:

  • The feature eliminates the need for long-lived "Remember me" cookies on the identity provider, which are a security concern and not universally available.
  • It is based on short-lived, one-time use SSO tokens issued and validated by SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication, which acts as the common trust anchor.
  • The feature is optional and in control by the customer: an administrator (de-/) activates it via a feature flag in SAP Mobile Services Admin Cockpit of Joule Work mobile app and controls which web applications participate via the Native-Web Trust configuration in SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication.
  • SAP Build Work Zone web UIs and tunneled embedded business apps are automatically covered. Additional apps can be added with a few clicks.
  • The feature is compatible with all in-app browser variants in Joule Work mobile app and all trusted web applications, regardless of whether they are SAP solutions or custom apps.

If you need further assistance configuring and making use of this new feature in the Joule Work mobile app, feel free to contact our product management team using jouleworkmobile@sap.com, which will be able to suggest the next steps for your scenario.

Further Reading

  • Switching to SAP Cloud Identity Services – Identity Authentication (SAP Help)

entry.title: Building a Compelling Learning Experience in SAP Work Zone
entry.content:
If you're running SAP SuccessFactors Work Zone alongside SAP SuccessFactors Learning, you've already got the foundation for one of the strongest learning experience setups in enterprise software. Work Zone gives you the unified workspace. SuccessFactors Learning gives you the system of record. The standard out-of-the-box LMS integration cards put learning functionality directly into the Work Zone experience: Learning Plan, Learning History, Goals, Curricula Status, My Classes, Learning Recommendations, Manager Approvals

 

That's solid. It's structured, reliable access to your SuccessFactors Learning data, surfaced where your people already work.

But there's a question worth asking. Does that meet the needs of the modern learner? And does it justify standing up a Work Zone layer at all, if Work Zone is only being used as a light-touch surface for SuccessFactors Learning?

The three layers, named

It helps to name the three layers explicitly.

SAP SuccessFactors Learning is the system of record. It holds your courses, your compliance trails, your assignments and your completions. It is the backbone — and it is not going away.

SAP Work Zone is the canvas. It pulls SuccessFactors data, SharePoint, Teams and other systems into a single, unified workspace for the employee. It is the place where work — and learning — converge.

The experience layer is what sits between the learner and the content. It is the difference between seeing a list of assignments and being guided through a learning journey. It is what determines whether your LMS is something employees are told to use or something they actually want to use.

For many organisations, the standard Work Zone LMS cards quietly become this third layer by default. That is where the opportunity sits.

What standard cards do — and where they stop

Standard cards expose SuccessFactors Learning data. They list. They link. They surface.

They do not curate. They do not personalise. They do not recommend beyond SuccessFactors. They do not host the social, gamified, journey-based behaviours that move adoption and completion rates.

 

Concretely, with standard cards alone:

  • The catalog appears as a flat list — no interactive search or visual discovery
  • There is no welcome experience and no personalisation
  • No trending content, no recommendations from network or peers
  • No playlists, tracks, or learning journeys
  • No gamification, knowledge checks, or social interactions on content
  • No path to layer in Skills and Talent Intelligence Hub content alongside learning
  • Managers appear only as approvers, not as part of the experience

If your L&D strategy is compliance and completion, standard cards may be enough. If your strategy includes capability, engagement and skills-led growth, they aren't.

What Blend LXP adds on top of Work Zone + SuccessFactors Learning

This is where Blend LXP earns its place. Built natively for the SuccessFactors Learning + Work Zone stack and co-developed with global enterprise customers, it picks up where the standard cards stop. The shape of the value sits in six areas.

Personalisation. A welcome experience tuned to the individual. Trending content based on interests. Recently accessed items, bookmarks, and recommendations that go beyond what SuccessFactors alone can see.

Discovery and search. Interactive catalog browse instead of a flat list. Smart search across SuccessFactors Learning, SharePoint, Teams, LinkedIn Learning, Coursera and other content sources. Featured Content, Featured Topics and Upcoming Events as first-class objects, not afterthoughts.

Curated learning experiences. Pre-filtered widgets, Playlists, Tracks, Learning Journeys — the building blocks L&D teams use to design for campaigns, audiences and moments of need rather than dumping everything in a single catalog.

Engagement and gamification. Points, badges, leaderboards, knowledge checks, social interactions on courses (like, recommend, share), and recommendations from peers and network. These are not nice-to-haves; they are the levers that materially move adoption and completion rates.

Manager surface. A team dashboard, manager views of learning plans, record-learning on behalf of the team. Managers become part of the experience, not just self-service onlookers.

Skills. Surface skills-tagged content, skills-aligned recommendations, and skills progress alongside the rest of the learning experience. As Talent Intelligence Hub and skills-based talent strategies move to centre stage, this is where the L&D and skills agendas converge.

Standard cards expose data. Blend LXP turns data into behaviour.

 

Build it yourself? Think twice.

One of Work Zone's real strengths is that it gives you the tools to build custom integration cards and apps. For many use cases — internal tools, niche workflows, departmental dashboards — that's exactly the right answer.

A learning experience platform is rarely one of them.

The reason is the pace of change. Personalisation engines, AI-driven recommendations, multi-source content aggregation, gamification, social learning, Skills tagging, GenAI authoring, agentic AI — these are all moving fast. Building custom means signing up to chase that roadmap with your own team, every quarter, indefinitely.

This is where the economics of SaaS earn their place. A purpose-built LXP like Blend LXP brings continuous capability gains without your team writing a line of code or owning the upgrade. The roadmap is somebody else's job. The feature gap shrinks rather than grows.

The other side of the same coin is technical baggage. Every custom integration card or app you build becomes something you have to maintain — across SAP upgrades, security reviews, browser changes, accessibility standards, language localisation. Multiply that across the surface area of a real learning experience — personalisation, search, content aggregation, gamification, social, manager dashboards, Skills tagging, AI — and you're staring at a perpetual development programme inside a part of HR that typically runs lean.

The build-vs-buy question for the experience layer isn't can we? It's should we? And for most organisations the right answer is to buy the experience layer and let engineering capacity go to the things only you can build.

Three recent capabilities worth a fresh look

Blend LXP has not stood still over the last two years. Three additions in particular materially change what's possible on top of the SuccessFactors + Work Zone stack.

Auto-tagging all content with Skills. Every video, document and course in Blend LXP is tagged automatically against your skills framework. This eliminates a long-standing operational overhead — the slow, manual content-tagging step that has historically blocked skills-based learning at scale. With it solved, the path from "skills strategy" to "skills running in the learner's daily experience" gets dramatically shorter.

Content tracking and resume on informal content. Tracking engagement on videos, PDFs and documents — and letting learners pick up exactly where they left off — adds a real engagement layer to the informal content that doesn't live inside formal courses. For organisations where the majority of learning happens outside formal courses, this is significant.

GenAI content creation with one-click translation. Create learning content with GenAI, then translate into Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese and other languages with a single click. Build fast, localise for your audience, ship in days not weeks. This changes the economics of content for global learning teams.

Each of these would have been a standalone roadmap item two years ago. In Blend LXP, they ship today.

 

What's next

Blend LXP's roadmap goes further. Agentic AI capabilities are opening up a dynamic, chat-based learning experience. Intelligent Q&A lets learners ask, and the platform answers from your own content. Scenario-based simulations move learning from consumption to deliberate practice.

The point isn't any individual feature. The point is that the experience layer is moving fast — and the distance between "standard cards" and "what Blend LXP makes possible" is widening, not closing.

The question worth asking

If your organisation runs SuccessFactors Learning and Work Zone today, there is a quiet decision sitting in front of you.

You can let the standard LMS integration cards be your experience layer. That is a viable choice, especially for compliance-led L&D strategies where the goal is structured access to assignments and completions. Your learners get a list. The list is accurate.

Or you can ask whether your learners deserve more than a list — and look at what Blend LXP, sitting on top of SuccessFactors Learning and Work Zone, makes possible. Personalisation, journeys, gamification, social, manager engagement, skills, and now AI — integrated into the Work Zone experience your people already use every day.

 

It's a question only your organisation can answer. But it is worth answering deliberately, not by default.

TalenTeam is an SAP SuccessFactors specialist partner and one of the earliest Work Zone implementation partners in the ecosystem. Blend LXP is our flagship Learning Experience Platform, co-developed with customers including GSK, with Vodafone and Scotia Bank as ongoing roadmap contributors. I

entry.title: SBPA Multiple Approval Levels: Fixed Steps or Reusable Loop? Suggestions please!!
entry.content:
Hi SAP Community,

I would like to get expert guidance on the best-practice approach for modelling a multi-level approval workflow in SAP Build Process Automation (SBPA).

We have a business process where the approval flow may go through around 18 sequential approval levels/personas.

In the current design discussion, there are two possible approaches.

Requirement

Most approval levels are using the same custom UI5 approval form.

The differences between the approval levels are mainly:

  • Current approver / approval level

  • Editable or non-editable fields based on the level

  • Routing to the next approver

  • Visibility of some fields or sections based on role/level

The common approval actions are mostly the same:

  • Approve

  • Reject

  • Send back / rework, if applicable

  • Add comments

Approach 1: Separate Approval Steps in SBPA

In this approach, each approval level is created as a separate approval step in SBPA.

For example:

  • Approval Step 1

  • Approval Step 2

  • Approval Step 3

  • …

  • Approval Step 18

Each step may call the same UI5 form, but the context mapping and routing are maintained separately in SBPA.

The advantage is that the process is visually clear and each approval stage is explicitly visible in the process model.

However, the concern is that this creates many repeated steps, repeated context mappings, and higher maintenance effort. In our case, we are also facing SBPA platform context-related issues because of the large number of repeated steps and mappings the browser is craching while opening the steps in SBPA platform.

Approach 2: Reusable Approval Step with Loop / Level-Based Routing

In this approach, we use a reusable approval step or a smaller number of approval steps.

A local process variable, such as currentApprovalLevel, is used to identify the current level.

The approver is determined dynamically based on the current level using API/master data/ECC OData.

After one approval is completed, the process checks whether another approval level is required. If yes, it moves to the next approval level and reuses the same approval step.

Example:

  1. currentApprovalLevel = 1

  2. Determine Level 1 approver

  3. Create approval task

  4. On approval, increment the approval level

  5. Determine the next approver

  6. Continue until all required approval levels are completed

The advantage is that it avoids repeating the same approval step many times when the UI form and approval behavior are the same.

The concern raised is that this may reduce process visibility and auditability if different personas have different business rules, SLA, rejection paths, escalation logic, or parallel approvals.

Main Question

From an SAP Build Process Automation best-practice perspective, which approach is recommended when many approval levels use the same UI5 form and mostly the same approval behavior?

Should all approval levels be modelled as explicit separate SBPA steps, even if the same form and same approval pattern are repeated?

Or is it acceptable to use a reusable approval step with loop/level-based routing for repeated same-pattern approval levels?

Additional Clarification

We are not trying to move the complete business process logic outside SBPA.

For approval stages that have different behavior, such as different UI, different SLA, different rejection path, different escalation logic, different business rules, or parallel approval, we understand that those should be modelled as separate SBPA steps.

The question is mainly about repeated approval levels where the behavior is the same and only the approver level, field editability, and routing change.

Would a hybrid approach be better, where different business stages are modelled separately, but repeated same-pattern approval levels are handled using reusable approval logic?

I would appreciate your guidance and suggestions based on SAP Build Process Automation best practices.

Thanks in advance.

SAP Build Process Automation SAP Intelligent Robotic Process Automation SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization

entry.title: SAP Build Work Zone + SAP Service Cloud V2: Creating a True Single Entry Point for Customer Service
entry.content:
Introduction

In today's enterprise landscape, employees often need to navigate multiple applications to complete a single business process. Service agents switch between CRM systems, ERP applications, workflow tools, and custom applications throughout the day, resulting in fragmented user experiences and reduced productivity.

The vision of a Unified Digital Workplace is simple: provide users with a single entry point where they can access all relevant applications, data, workflows, and insights based on their role.

SAP Build Work Zone has become the strategic digital workplace solution for SAP customers. Organizations already leverage Work Zone as a central access point for solutions such as SAP S/4HANA, SAP SuccessFactors, and custom SAP BTP applications.

Now, the same experience can be extended to customer-facing teams by integrating SAP Service Cloud Version 2 (V2) into SAP Build Work Zone, enabling service agents and managers to work from a single, personalized workspace.

In this blog, we will explore the business value, architecture, implementation approach, and a demo scenario showcasing how SAP Build Work Zone and SAP Service Cloud V2 can work together seamlessly.

A Short Story

Meet Prasad, a Customer Service Manager at a global manufacturing company running SAP's full suite.

Every morning, Prasad logs into SAP Build Work Zone. On her home page, she sees her personalized tiles: open production orders from S/4HANA, pending approvals from SuccessFactors, and her team's KPI dashboard. Everything is in one place.

But then her phone rings. A key customer is escalating a service ticket — a machine breakdown at their site. Prasad switches to a completely different browser tab, logs into SAP Service Cloud V2 separately, searches for the customer, finds the ticket, checks the service history, and tries to correlate it with the spare parts availability from S/4HANA — which means another tab, another login.

Three systems. Three tabs. One frustrated manager. One unhappy customer.

This is the problem SAP Build Work Zone + SAP Service Cloud V2 integration solves.

After the integration, Prasad's Work Zone home page now has a dedicated Service Operations section. The Service Cloud V2 app is embedded as a tile and a full sidebar integration. She can:

  • See real-time ticket queue directly from the Work Zone homepage
  • Open and update service tickets without leaving Work Zone
  • WorkZone can Receive intelligent notifications when ticket SLA thresholds are breached

Her morning is now seamless. Her customer gets faster resolution. Her team is more productive.

That is the power of a single entry point.

Key Benefits

True Single Entry Point for All Personas

Persona                                                             Before                                                                          After

Service Agent

2 systems (Work Zone + Service Cloud)

1 — Work Zone

Service Manager

3 systems (Work Zone + Service Cloud + S/4HANA)

1 — Work Zone

IT Admin

Manage 3 separate portals

Manage 1 unified portal

Executive

Multiple dashboards

1 personalized command center

Key Benefits

  • Unified User Experience:  Access SAP Service Cloud V2, SAP S/4HANA, SAP SuccessFactors, and custom applications through one portal.
  • Single Sign-On :Reduce authentication complexity and improve user productivity.
  • Role-Based Access: Deliver personalized content, applications, and workflows based on user roles.
  • Improved Productivity: Minimize context switching between applications and browser tabs.
  • Extensibility: Integrate custom SAPUI5 and SAP BTP applications alongside standard SAP solutions.

Why bring Service Cloud V2 into Work Zone

 

How to surface SAP Service Cloud V2 in Work Zone

  • Subscribe to SAP Build Work Zone, standard or advanced edition

In your BTP subaccount, go to Service Marketplace and subscribe to SAP Build Work Zone. Advanced Edition is required if you need Digital Workplace Service features (content federation, external solutions). Standard is sufficient for most SAP Cloud app integrations.

 
Navigation path: BTP Cockpit → Subaccount → Service Marketplace → SAP Build Work Zone → Create subscription → choose edition → Assign role collections Launchpad_Admin and Launchpad_User to relevant users.

  • Create a destination for SAP Service Cloud V2

Work Zone discovers external SaaS apps through BTP Destinations. SAP Service Cloud V2 exposes OData and REST APIs under its tenant URL. Create a destination with OAuth2 client credentials so Work Zone can fetch app descriptors and launch URLs securely.

Destination config (key fields)

Name: SCV2
Type: HTTP · URL: https://<your-tenant>.crm.cloud.sap
Auth: OAuth2ClientCredentials
Token Service URL: IAS token endpoint
Additional Properties: HTML5.DynamicDestination = true, sap-platform = cf

  • Add Service Cloud V2 as a content provider in Work Zone

Now tell Work Zone where to find those deployed apps. Open the Work Zone Site Manager and register Service Cloud V2 as a content provider. Point it at the HTML5 App Repository app and the SCV2 destination. Work Zone will fetch the CDM and expose the tiles to administrators.

Navigation path

Work Zone Site Manager → Channel Manager → Add → SAP BTP → Content Provider Name: SAP Service Cloud V2 → Runtime Destination: SCV2 → Design-Time Destination: SCV2 → Fetch content → Save.

  • Assign Service Cloud tiles to roles and groups

After fetching content, the Service Cloud V2 tiles appear in the Content Manager under "Available Content". Assign them to a role (e.g., ServiceAgent) and add that role to a launchpad group. 

Navigation path : Work Zone Content Manager → Add to Role → Create/select role ServiceAgent → Assign group Service Cloud Apps → Publish site.
 

See it in action — one launchpad, everything connected

To demonstrate the integration capabilities of SAP Build Work Zone, i created a simple demo showcasing how different applications can be brought together through a unified user experience.

In this video , users can observe the following:

  • Sales Cloud and Service Cloud V2 Integration
    SAP Build Work Zone provides direct access to Sales and Service Cloud V2, allowing users to launch these applications seamlessly from a single location.
  • Access to Business Objects
    Users can navigate to important business objects such as Accounts and Cases directly from Work Zone, reducing the need to switch between multiple systems.
  • Custom Application Integration
    Custom applications, including SAPUI5 applications deployed on SAP BTP, can be embedded within Work Zone and accessed alongside standard SAP applications.
  • Cross-Application Navigation
    The same custom application embedded in Work Zone can also be accessed from Service Cloud V2, enabling a connected and consistent user journey across platforms.

Why This Matters

By bringing together SAP applications and custom solutions, SAP Build Work Zone becomes a true single entry point for users. Whether users need to access Service Cloud V2, Sales Cloud, business data, or custom applications, everything is available through a unified digital workplace.

This approach simplifies navigation, improves productivity, and delivers a more seamless user experience by reducing the need to manage multiple entry points and disconnected systems.

Conclusion

Organizations often struggle with users navigating across multiple applications and portals. With SAP Build Work Zone, businesses can create a centralized experience that connects SAP solutions and custom applications under one roof. The result is a more intuitive, efficient, and user-friendly workspace that helps employees focus on their work rather than searching for the right application.

entry.title: What’s New in SAP Build: Q1 & Q2 2026 Release Highlights
entry.content:
Greetings, Builders! We blinked and just like that, the first half of 2026 is complete. There’s been a whirlwind of updates, including our recent announcement at SAPPHIRE of the new Joule Studio for intent-based development and agent creation.

Q1 and Q2 also brought a wave of innovations across SAP Build, helping our users extend and automate applications faster than ever. From AI-powered capabilities in SAP Build Work Zone, Joule Work Mobile, CAP, and SAPUI5, to improved visibility in process automation and more, these enhancements address some of your key pain points around developer productivity, simplified workflows, and user experience. Here are the Q1 and Q2 2026 release highlights from SAP Build, plus a look ahead at the new Joule Studio and how you can start learning the fundamentals of AI Agent building today.

Improved Customization and Gen AI in SAP Build Work Zone

No, it's not a social networking site from 2003, it's personalized, relevant SAP content.

Easy access to personalized content with My Space

Following the clear feedback from customers, it’s now possible to organize and manage your favorite Work Zone content on a dedicated, personal page. Many business users often have multiple roles, which may include content spanned across various spaces and structures. The “My Space” capability lets you bring all of that together on one page, allowing you to quickly access your relevant content and easily edit it to fit your specific needs.

👉 Learn more in the blog post by @ThomasHensel

Enhanced text generation and refinement with AI

The text widget toolbar now includes an AI option to generate text for the widget. In addition, AI can refine the text in input fields, text areas, and text widgets. This includes changing the tone of the text, adjusting its length, and fixing spelling and grammar.

Create whole workspaces, locate relevant content and more with Joule

At the end of last year, Joule became integrated into SAP Build Work Zone, advanced edition, bringing the AI assistant’s conversational intelligence right to your workspace. Now, Joule supports three new, frequently used scenarios:

  • Transactional: Create workspaces based on templates, upload content, or invite users to become members.
  • Navigational: Search for specific workspaces that you manage or are related to keywords.
  • Informational: Search for a specific user and show their profile.

You can trigger each of these scenarios through the familiar conversational experience with Joule, executing more tasks and finding key information faster.

👉 See example prompts and learn more on the Help Portal.

👉 See all the latest releases from SAP Build Work Zone.

Updates in Mobile: Seamless SSO, end-user support, MDK 26.6 & more

SAP Mobile Start’s rebranding, enhanced Joule and improved single sign-on

SAP Mobile Start has been the established native mobile entry point for your company’s systems and daily tasks, including content from SAP Build Work Zone. The app has now been rebranded as the Joule Work mobile app. While the core functionalities remain the same as before, the new app includes an updated Joule icon, full-screen interface, and voice dictation of prompts. 

With version 3.0, Joule Work mobile app also introduces a streamlined single sign-on for opening web applications in the in-app browser. For organizations with large mobile workforces, this eliminates the need for repetitive credential entry and creates a seamless workflow across applications. Learn more about these updates in the blog posts by @ThiloBerndt and @thomas-bruckner.

  • SAP Mobile Start - Rebranding of the app, enhanced Joule and improved single sign-on functionality
  • Joule Work mobile app version 3.1 is out
  • Seamless Mobile-to-Web Single Sign-On with the Joule Work mobile app

Customizing in-app support for end users in Joule Work

Getting technical support for mobile app issues is a common frustration that often causes users to turn to the wrong channels, such as app store reviews or generic feedback forms. It’s now possible for companies to add support information, such as contact details, ticketing systems and resources, directly to your Joule Work mobile app and configure it in SAP Mobile Services. This enhancement transforms how your end users can access help when they need it most.

👉 Learn more in the blog post by @ivan_chaushev.

AI feedback forms, extended compliance checks and more in MDK Client 26.6

The latest release of Mobile development kit (MDK) is now available, bringing several significant upgrades to security, compliance and embedded AI in native mobile app development. Device compliance checks have now been extended to before a user onboards, allowing for earlier detection of compromised devices and stronger security. Enhancements to AI are also ongoing, including a new control that enables quick user feedback on AI-generated content.

👉 See the complete list of new MDK features in this blog post by @Jitendra_Kansal.

New CAP plugins for AI recommendations & improved traceability

RPT-1 generated recommendations with CAP AI plugin for node.js 

In pro-code development, SAP Cloud Application Programming (CAP) continues to provide productivity gains by allowing developers to reduce boilerplate code and focus on problem solving. The new SAP CAP AI plugin for node.js provides recommendations powered by RPT-1 within the in-app UI. The plugin supports multi-tenancy, simplifies AI Core configuration, and inherently embeds the enterprise readiness of CAP out-of-the-box.

👉 Learn more in the blog post by @rupamaity.

New and improved change tracking plugin

Version 2.0 of the change tracking plugin for CAP has been released and brings major improvements to how enterprise applications capture and visualize data changes. The new version includes tree table visualization, support for CDS Expression Language (CXL), and a fundamentally redesigned architecture. These changes bring significant upgrades to performance and traceability, allowing developers to exercise more control over changes and customizations.

👉 Learn more in the blog post by @rupamaity.

Streamlined SAPUI5 development with AI and developer extensibility

UI5 plugins for modernization and coding agents in GitHub Copilot

Keeping your SAPUI5 app up to date just got easier. The new UI5 Modernization Plugin automates the most time-consuming parts of app modernization: replacing deprecated APIs, eliminating global namespaces, and much more. The plugin is available for Claude Code as well as GitHub Copilot. Also now available for GitHub Copilot are UI5 Plugins for Coding Agents (previously known as UI5 Plugins for Claude). These bring up-to-date SAPUI5 knowledge directly into your AI-assisted development workflow.

The latest version of the UI5 MCP Server is also now available and supports the development of UI Integration Cards. It includes three new tools to assist Large Language Models (LLMs) in creating new cards from scratch or editing existing ones, following the best practices for card development. Learn more about these plugins:

  • Introducing the UI5 Modernization Plugin: Modernize Your OpenUI5/SAPUI5 App in Hours, Not Weeks
  • UI5 Plugins for Coding Agents: Now Supporting GitHub Copilot
  • UI5 MCP Server Got Extended for UI Integration Cards Generation

Key User Adaptation & Transitions for UI5 TypeScript developers

With key user adaptation, business users can change the UI of SAP Fiori standard apps directly in the runtime app. If more complex changes are needed, there now is a seamless transition from key user to developer extensibility in SAP Build.

TypeScript is going through its biggest transition in years. If you build SAPUI5 applications with TypeScript, we have provided a guide for developers around these changes.

👉 Learn more about key user adaptation and the TypeScript transition.

Extended visibility and proactive monitoring in process automation

Avoid manual error-tracing with automated exception handling.

Enhanced process visibility with instance-level attributes

Operational teams often lack business context in process monitoring. For a business user, this can make it difficult to see key details like approaching deadlines or decisions taken by the previous approver. Now with more instance-level attributes enabled: Active Step - Upcoming due date and Last Step Outcome, you can add more meaningful context to process instances, allowing users to easily search, filter, group, and analyze processes where a step is due soon. This allows teams to improve their decision-making and reduce the risk of breaching SLAs.

👉 Learn more about instance-level attributes in the Help Portal.

Process group connections & other updates

More updates are now available in process automation, focused on improved visibility, proactive monitoring, and enhanced governance. Here are some highlights:

  • Process group connections (1-to-many): Organizations often need visibility across related processes, not just individual workflows. This enables end-to-end monitoring by linking a primary process with its associated downstream processes, providing a more complete view of business execution.
  • Notifications in Visibility Scenarios: Proactive email alerts notify users about processing failures, skipped instances, or event thresholds before they impact operations. This reduces manual monitoring and helps teams respond to issues faster.
  • Environment Filters: New controls allow users to view or restrict process visibility by environment. This improves governance and makes it easier to manage and analyze process data across development, test, and production landscapes.
  • Event handler to catch Action errors: Introduces configurable Retry mechanisms and structured exception handling at the Action level. This allows organizations to systematically manage errors, while reducing manual and time-consuming troubleshooting efforts.

👉 See all the latest releases and documentation on the Help Portal.

Looking ahead to the new Joule Studio

If you're looking to learn more about the new Joule Studio and how you can use it to start creating AI agents, we have great news: the learning journey Introducing Joule Studio is now available! With this free course, you'll be able to understand the bigger picture and how Joule Studio fits into SAP Business AI Platform. You'll also get to know what you can do with Joule Studio and Joule Work, how you can use it to create agents and automate workflows with n8n.

entry.title: Simplified user management option(s) for SAP Build Work Zone
entry.content:
Motivation & Goal

User management for SAP Build Work Zone often starts simple, but becomes more complex once real-life landscape requirements come into play. Customers typically need to bring together SAP Cloud Identity Services, SAP BTP role collections, SAP Cloud Identity Provisioning jobs, and the Digital Workplace Service (DWS) user store within Work Zone. Depending on the setup, this may also include different user types, identity providers, and integrations such as SAP Task Center.

With the latest SAP Build Work Zone enhancements in the area of user management, this setup becomes simpler in two specific aspects:

  1. A simplified option where company administrator and read-only administrator permissions are derived from the already required SAP BTP role collections, without an additional local assignment in DWS.
  2. An option to automatically create users during login and update selected user attributes on every subsequent login, in addition to the existing Identity Provisioning-based user synchronisation approach.

The goal is not to replace existing provisioning options. Identity Provisioning remains the right choice for many lifecycle-management scenarios. The new options provide a faster setup path where the required user information is already available during login, reducing mandatory setup effort for common scenarios across SAP Build Work Zone, advanced edition and SAP SuccessFactors Work Zone.

What changes with the new user setup options

Before looking at the new options, let's quickly recap the previous setup pattern. User data typically had to exist not only on SAP BTP and in SAP Cloud Identity Services, but also in the built-in user store inside Work Zone. In most implementations, this was handled through Identity Provisioning jobs that transferred attributes such as user name, email address, first name, last name, user type, and additional attributes. This approach remains valid, but for initial setup and many standard use cases it also meant an additional provisioning flow before users could access Work Zone.

The Administration Console now includes a dedicated User Setup Options section. For new SAP Build Work Zone tenants, the default setup follows the simplified third option: company administrator and read-only administrator permissions can be derived from the already required SAP BTP role collections, automatic internal user creation is enabled by default, and automatic external user creation remains available as an optional feature. External user creation was already supported; the new part is the default login-based creation and update flow for internal users, together with Global User ID support for both user types.

Company and read-only administrators derived from SAP BTP role collections

The first option partially removes duplicate administrator assignment effort. SAP BTP role collections were and remain required. Previously, company administrator and read-only administrator permissions also required an additional local assignment inside Work Zone. With this enhancement, SAP Build Work Zone can derive these two permissions directly from the relevant role collections, for example Workzone_Admin or HR_Workzone_Admin. Customers still assign the required role collection in SAP BTP as before; what is no longer needed is the additional Work Zone local step.

During login, SAP Build Work Zone evaluates the assigned roles. If the token contains the relevant administrator role, the corresponding permission is reflected. If the role collection assignment is removed, the derived permission is removed as well (with the subsequent logout/login). This does not introduce a new authorization source. It simply removes the need to maintain the same company administrator or read-only administrator intent twice: once through SAP BTP role collections and again locally in Work Zone.

Other permissions remain intentionally local in Work Zone. This includes page content administrators, support administrators, and administrative area assignments.

For existing tenants, administrators should review the current setup before switching to this option. The relevant SAP BTP role collection assignments should already reflect who is supposed to receive company administrator or read-only administrator permissions, because these assignments become the source from which Work Zone derives the two permissions. The same role-collection-based concept also connects well with previously delivered workspace access control enhancements, where workspace visibility and read-only access can be controlled for selected users, user lists, or role collections.

Automatic user creation and update during login

The second feature is about user creation and recurring updates during login. SAP Build Work Zone can create or update users based on attributes included in the token. When the user logs in, the system checks whether the matching SCIM user already exists. If not, the user is created directly during login. If the user already exists, selected attributes can be refreshed with the values from the current login.

For new tenants, automatic internal user creation is enabled by default. When an internal user logs in for the first time, SAP Build Work Zone creates the user automatically; on later logins, supported attributes are updated again. External user creation was already supported, and remains optional. If enabled, SAP Build Work Zone only creates an external user automatically if the token contains the Workzone_External_User role collection assignment.

The Global User ID provides a stable identifier across SAP technology layers, products, and integration scenarios. In SAP Build Work Zone, this is especially relevant for scenarios such as SAP Task Center integration and for combining login-based user creation with SCIM API-based provisioning. If the user_uuid attribute is included in the token, Work Zone can handle it during automatic creation and update for internal and external users. The same identifier can then act as the checkpoint for provisioning jobs that enrich the automatically created baseline profile with additional attributes or groups.

At the same time, customers should still carefully validate their identity setup. The Global User ID should be stable and unique, and customers using SAP Cloud Identity Services should follow the recommended approach for generating and distributing it across their landscape. Identity Provisioning remains the right choice when customers need scheduled or event-driven user lifecycle management, centralized transformation logic, provisioning to multiple target systems, pre-creation before first login, advanced administration of user attributes and groups, or integration with a broader identity governance process.

The practical impact is mainly visible during initial setup: fewer mandatory provisioning steps, less duplicate administrator maintenance, and clearer defaults for internal and external user creation. In the Work Zone configurator flow, you can now treat the IPS setup as optional where login-based user creation already provides the required user information.

Configuration considerations

Before changing these options in an existing tenant, administrators should review the current configuration carefully. For administrator access, the SAP BTP role collection assignments should correctly reflect the intended company administrator and read-only administrator users. For automatic user creation and update, the application trust in SAP Cloud Identity should contain the required attributes, including user_uuid, email address, given name, and family name. Customers combining login-based handling with SCIM API-based provisioning must use the same Global User ID and SCIM.userName across both flows . For external users, the Workzone_External_User role collection must be assigned correctly.

Additional Read

The following resources provide more details on the individual building blocks mentioned above:

  • User Setup Options for SAP Build Work Zone, advanced edition
  • Allow SAML Assertion-Based Creation of External Users
  • De-mystifying SAP Cloud Identity Services Integration with SAP Build Work Zone
  • Access Control Options in SAP Build Work Zone, advanced edition
  • Create Workspace Accessible to Selected Users/Roles with Read Only Mode

entry.title: From Blank Canvas to Branded Launchpad: Configuring SAP Build Work Zone, Advanced Edition
entry.content:
From Blank Canvas to Branded Launchpad: Configuring SAP Build Work Zone, Advanced Edition

A few months ago, I was handed a fresh SAP Build Work Zone, Advanced Edition tenant and a one-line brief: "Make this the front door for all our Fiori and S/4HANA apps, and make it look like us, not like SAP."

No pressure.

If you've been through a BWZ AE setup before, you know the official documentation is thorough — almost too thorough. It's scattered across Site Manager, Theme Designer, Channel Manager, and half a dozen BTP Cockpit screens, and it's easy to lose the thread of why you're clicking where you're clicking. This post is my attempt to walk through the parts of the configuration that actually took time to get right — site settings, theming, the home page, S/4HANA federation, and app visibility.

I'm assuming your subaccount, trust configuration, and booster are already sorted (that's its own topic). Let's pick up from an activated tenant and take it all the way to a live, branded, federated launchpad.

1. Getting the Site Settings Right

Everything an end user sees and does at runtime — the header, the navigation, search, notifications, theming — is controlled from Site Settings. It's the first place I go after a fresh site is created, because a lot of the "why doesn't this feature show up" questions later trace back to a toggle here.

Open Site Manager → Site Directory, either open your existing default site or create a new one (name, description, default language, template), and click the gear icon on the site tile.

[Insert image here: Site Directory screen with the site tile and the Site Settings gear icon highlighted]

A few sections worth knowing well:

Section What it controls
GeneralSite name, description, default language, time zone — your branding and locale defaults
LaunchpadApp finder, notifications, search bar, "Me Area" menu, sign-out, recent activity
ThemeDefault theme, whether users can switch themes, which themes are available
Spaces & PagesWhether you're running modern Spaces navigation or classic Groups
SearchEnterprise search on/off, providers, categories
NotificationsNotification service and polling interval (needed for the Fiori notifications channel)
SAP CompanionContextual help toggle and parameters
MobileMobile site, mobile theme, app icon
Custom CSS/HTMLLightweight branding via injected CSS/HTML in header and footer, without full theming

One thing that caught me out early on: some toggles — theme switching and Spaces, in particular — only appear once the corresponding feature is licensed and enabled at the subscription level. If a setting is "missing," check licensing before you assume it's a bug.

Whenever you change something here, Save first, then Publish the site to push it to the runtime URL, then actually open that URL to confirm the change landed. It sounds obvious, but skipping the "open the URL and look" step is how half of the "it's not working" tickets get created.

2. Making It Look Like You (Theme Designer)

Branding is usually the part stakeholders care about most and engineers enjoy least. The UI Theme Designer makes it manageable: you take a standard SAP theme (Morning Horizon, Horizon, Quartz) and create what SAP calls a Z-copy — your own editable version — rather than touching the original.

You can reach it from Site Manager → Channel Manager, or directly via BTP Cockpit → Instances & Subscriptions → UI Theme Designer (you'll need the subscription active and the Workzone_Advanced_Theming role assigned).

To start: New Theme → Base Theme (e.g., SAP Morning Horizon) → Theme ID starting with Z (e.g., Z_Acme_Horizon) → Theme Name → Vendor → Create.

[Insert image here: Theme Designer "New Theme" dialog with a base theme selected]

From there, the guided panels cover most of what you'll need:

  • Quick – brand color, accent color, base text color, header bar (fastest path to "on-brand")
  • Basic Colors – brand, highlight, page background, content/panel background, line color
  • Fiori 3 / Horizon – shell header, brand color, tile background, button colors
  • Images – company logo, favicon, login background
  • Fonts – font family and size scale (custom fonts need to be uploaded as CSS)
  • Expert – per-control LESS variables, for when the guided panels don't go deep enough
  • CSS Code Editor – raw CSS overrides for anything the parameters don't expose

That last one is where I ended up spending the most time. For example, getting rounded, slightly elevated tiles took nothing more than:

 
css
.sapMGT, .sapUshellTile {
  border-radius: 12px !important;
  box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,.08);
}

Use the Preview dropdown in the top right to check how it looks against the Launchpad, a Fiori app, and Build Work Zone itself — they don't always render identically.

Once you're happy: Save (draft), then Save & Publish. Then go back to Site Manager → Site Settings → Theme, add your Z-theme to Available Themes, set it as Default if that's the plan, and Save → Publish the site again.

The one rule I'd underline twice: never edit a standard SAP theme directly. SAP upgrades can silently overwrite or lock it. Always work on a Z-copy.

3. Designing a Home Page People Actually Want to Land On

This is where the site stops being a shell and starts being a product. The Page Designer is what lets you assemble sections and widgets — tiles, news feeds, quick links, images, custom HTML, workflow inboxes — into something that feels like a curated homepage rather than a generic app list.

Go to Site Manager → Workspace → Pages → + Create → Page, give it a title (e.g., "Home"), a description and ID, and pick a layout template (one column, two columns, or mixed).

Inside the canvas, + Add Section to create logical groupings (Quick Links, News, My Apps), then + Add Widget inside each section. The widget types worth knowing:

  • App Launchers — tiles backed by the catalog
  • Card / Smart Business KPI — Fiori cards
  • News / RSS feed
  • Image / Carousel — marketing visuals
  • HTML / Custom HTML — rich content
  • To-Do / My Inbox — workflow tasks
  • Workspace Cards — quick links into spaces or groups

Each widget gets configured individually (data source, target intent or URL, title, image), and you can drag to reorder both widgets and sections.

Once the page is saved, it needs a home: add it to a Space (Workspace → Spaces), then attach that Space to a Role (Workspace → Roles), and assign the Role to the right IAS user groups — for example, Workzone_End_User. Open the runtime site as a test user to confirm.

Worth remembering: whatever gets published on a page is visible to every end user with the assigned role. If you need persona-specific homepages — one for finance, one for warehouse staff — that means multiple pages and multiple roles, not one page trying to do everything.

4. Bringing S/4HANA In Without Rebuilding Everything (Federation)

This is the part that made the whole exercise worthwhile. Instead of recreating your entire Fiori catalog inside BWZ, federation lets the site consume apps and roles directly from your S/4HANA Front-End Server. A user clicks a tile in BWZ, and the request is proxied straight through to S/4HANA via a destination.

Before touching BTP, get the S/4HANA side ready:

  • Implement the relevant SAP Notes for content federation on the FES (check the current note for your release — these change).
  • Activate the OData service /UI2/PAGE_BUILDER_CUST and the federation service /UI2/INTEROP in SICF.
  • Set up a technical user with the equivalent of SAP_UI2_ADMIN / SAP_UI2_USER.
  • Establish trust between S/4HANA and the BTP subaccount — SAML 2.0, or Principal Propagation via Cloud Connector if it's on-premise.

With that in place, you'll typically create two destinations in BTP Cockpit (Connectivity → Destinations → New Destination):

Runtime destination (used to actually launch the apps):

Property Value
NameS4H_Runtime
TypeHTTP
URLhttps://<s4-fes-host>:<port>
Proxy TypeOnPremise (via Cloud Connector) or Internet
AuthenticationSAMLAssertion / PrincipalPropagation
Additional PropertiesHTML5.DynamicDestination=true, WebIDEEnabled=true, sap.applicationdevelopment.actions.enabled=true, sap.build.usage=ui_generation, html5.timeout=60000

Content-provider destination (for catalogs, groups, and roles):

Property Value
NameS4H_Content
TypeHTTP
URLhttps://<s4-fes-host>:<port>/sap/opu/odata/UI2/INTEROP
Proxy TypeOnPremise / Internet
AuthenticationBasicAuthentication (technical user) or PrincipalPropagation
Additional PropertiesHTML5.DynamicDestination=true, sap.content.providerType=SAPUI2, sap.business.service=content_provider

Back in Site Manager: Channel Manager → Content Channels → + Create Content Channel, choose SAP S/4HANA (or "SAP Systems"), point it to the S4H_Content destination, and give it a label like "S/4 Production."

Then, to actually pull the content across: open the channel, click Update Content — BWZ fetches the available catalogs, groups, and roles from S/4HANA. Switch to Content Manager → Content Explorer, select your S/4 provider, pick the roles or catalogs you want exposed, and Add to My Content. From that point, they show up under Workspace → Roles and get assigned to user groups exactly like locally-built roles.

If your S/4HANA is on-premise, this is also where SAP Cloud Connector and Principal Propagation earn their keep — you'll expose the FES host through a virtual-to-internal mapping to get true end-to-end SSO.

5. Controlling Who Sees What (Spaces, Catalogs, Groups, Roles)

If federation is the "how do apps get in," this is the "who's allowed to see them." The whole visibility model in BWZ comes down to one chain, and once it clicks, the rest of the configuration gets a lot less confusing:

App → Catalog → Page → Space → Role → User Group

For a custom app: build it in SAP Build Code or BAS, deploy it as an MTA into the same subaccount's HTML5 Application Repository, and BWZ will auto-detect it once deployed (check Site Manager → Channel Manager → HTML5 Apps for status "Available").

From there:

  • Catalog — Workspace → Catalogs → Create, give it a title/ID/description, then add your HTML5 or federated apps to it.
  • Group (optional, classic Launchpad only) — Workspace → Groups → Create, drag tiles in from the catalog. Only relevant if the site isn't running in Spaces mode.
  • Page — as covered above, references the catalog so its tiles become available.
  • Space — Workspace → Spaces → Create, then add the pages you want inside it, in order.
  • Role — Workspace → Roles → Create. On the Catalogs tab, assign the catalog (this is what grants app permission). On the Spaces tab, assign the space (this is what grants navigation visibility — these are two different things and it's easy to assign one and forget the other). On the Assignments tab, assign the IAS user groups. Save and Publish.

Before calling it done, run through this checklist with a real test user:

  • Open the site URL logged in as a user belonging to the right IAS group.
  • Confirm the Space shows up in top navigation (or the Space Selector).
  • Confirm the Page renders with its tiles and widgets.
  • Click a tile and confirm the federated S/4HANA or custom HTML5 app actually launches.

entry.title: Building Interactive SAPUI5 UI Integration Cards: From List Card to Object Card with local JSON data
entry.content:
Hi Everyone,

Today, I would like to share a blog about building interactive SAPUI5 UI Integration Cards using List and Object Cards with local JSON data.

SAPUI5 UI Integration Cards provide a lightweight and reusable way to display business information in a compact and visually appealing format. They can be embedded into SAP Fiori applications, SAP Build Work Zone, dashboards, and other SAP solutions to create rich and interactive user experiences.

In many business scenarios, users first view summarized information in a List Card and then need to access more detailed information. This is commonly known as the Master-Detail pattern. By combining a List Card with an inline Object Card using the ShowCard action, users can quickly navigate from a summary view to detailed information without leaving the current context.

In this blog, we will build an interactive SAPUI5 UI Integration Card application using local JSON data. We will create a List Card, configure an inline Object Card, and implement a Master-Detail experience using the ShowCard action. By the end of this blog, you will understand how to build interactive and reusable UI Integration Cards within a single card manifest.

 

Overview

SAPUI5 UI Integration Cards are reusable UI components that display business information in a compact format. They help developers build interactive dashboards and applications while keeping the UI clean and modular.

In this blog, we will use two card types:

  • List Card – Displays a collection of records in a summarized format.
  • Object Card – Displays detailed information about a selected record.

To make the application interactive, we will use the ShowCard action. When a user clicks an item in the List Card, an inline Object Card opens and displays the corresponding details, creating a Master-Detail experience.

For demonstration purposes, I am using an Employee example with local JSON data.

Step 1: Create a New SAPUI5 Application

Create a new SAPUI5 application using the SAP Fiori Application Generator in SAP Business Application Studio (BAS) or Visual Studio Code.

Select the following options:

  • Application Type: Basic SAPUI5 Application
  • Framework: SAPUI5
  • Minimum UI5 Version: 1.150.0
  • Project Name: intergrationuicards

After creating the project, the structure will look like:

 

Step 2: Add the UI Integration Library

UI Integration Cards are provided by the sap.ui.integration library.

Open:

webapp/manifest.json

Under:

sap.ui5
└── dependencies
              └── libs

Add the following library:

"sap.ui5": {
    "flexEnabled": true,
    "dependencies": {
      "minUI5Version": "1.150.0",
      "libs": {
        "sap.m": {},
        "sap.ui.core": {},
        "sap.ui.integration": {}  
      }
    },

This library enables the use of the Card control within SAPUI5 applications.

 

Step 3: Create the Required Project Structure

Inside the webapp folder, create the following folders:

webapp
│
├── cards
└── model

These folders will be used for:

  • cards – Stores the UI Integration Card manifest (cardManifest.json).
  • model – Stores the local JSON data (employees.json).

Note: You can refer to the project structure shown in the Step 1 screenshot to see where these folders should be created.

Inside the model folder, create a file named:

This JSON file acts as the data source for the List Card.

 

Step 5: Create the Card Manifest

Inside the cards folder, create a file named:

card/cardManifest.json

{

  "sap.app": {
    "id": "employee.card",

            },

                        "value": "{employee>/firstName}"
                      },
                      {
                        "label": "Last Name",
                        "value": "{employee>/lastName}"
                      },
                      {
                        "label": "Full Name",
                        "value": "{employee>/name}"
                      },
                      {
                        "label": "Gender",
                        "value": "{employee>/gender}"
                      }
                    ]
                  },
                  {
                    "title": "Professional Information",
                    "items": [
                      {
                        "label": "Department",
                        "value": "{employee>/department}"
                      },
                      {
                        "label": "Office Location",
                        "value": "{employee>/location}"
                      }
                    ]
                  }
                ]
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    },
    "header": {
      "title": "Employee List",
      "subTitle": "Explore departments and locations"
    },
    "content": {
      "data": {
        "request": {
          "url": "/model/employees.json"
        },
        "path": "/employees"
      },
      "item": {
        "icon": {
          "src": "{photo}",
          "shape": "Circle"
        },
        "title": "{firstName}",
        "description": "{location}",
        "actions": [
          {
            "type": "ShowCard",
            "parameters": {
              "childCardKey": "employeeDetail",
              "data": {
                "employee": {
                  "firstName": "{firstName}",
                  "lastName": "{lastName}",
                  "name": "{name}",
                  "gender": "{gender}",
                  "department": "{department}",
                  "location": "{location}",
                  "photo": "{photo}"
                }
              }
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    }
  }
}

This manifest contains the complete configuration for both the List Card and the inline Object Card. The List Card displays a summary of the available records, while the Object Card displays detailed information about the selected record. Instead of creating separate card manifests, the Object Card is defined as a child card within the same manifest and is displayed using the ShowCard action. This approach creates a simple Master-Detail experience within a single card configuration.

Understanding the Card Manifest


List Card

The List Card serves as the master view of the application, displaying a summary of the available records. It is configured using the sap.card section with the card type set to List.

The List Card includes the following sections:

  • Header – Displays the card title and subtitle.
  • Data Source – Loads data from the local employees.json file.
  • Item Template – Displays each record with a profile image, name, and location.
  • Click Action – Uses the ShowCard action to open the Object Card when a user selects a list item.

This provides users with a clean and interactive summary view of the available records.

Object Card

The Object Card serves as the detail view of the application and is defined as a child card using the configuration.childCards section.

When a user selects an item from the List Card, the selected data is passed to the Object Card, which displays detailed information such as:

  • First Name
  • Last Name
  • Full Name
  • Gender
  • Department
  • Office Location

For better readability, the information is organized into the following groups:

  • Personal Details
  • Professional Information


ShowCard Action

The ShowCard action connects the List Card with the Object Card.

When a user clicks a record in the List Card:

  • The selected record's data is passed to the child Object Card.
  • The ShowCard action automatically opens the Object Card.
  • The Object Card displays the detailed information for the selected record.

This provides a smooth Master-Detail navigation experience without requiring additional pages or routing.

 

Step 6: Display the Card in SAPUI5

Open:

View/App.view.xml

Import the UI Integration Card namespace and add the Card control.

<mvc:View
    controllerName="intergrationuicards.controller.App"
    displayBlock="true"
    xmlns:mvc="sap.ui.core.mvc"
    xmlns="sap.m"
    xmlns:card="sap.ui.integration.widgets">

    <App id="idApp">
        <pages>
            <Page id="idMainPage" title="UI Integration Card">

                <content>
                    <card:Card id="idEmployeeCard" manifest="/cards/cardManifest.json" width="400px"/>
                </content>

            </Page>
        </pages>
    </App>

</mvc:View>

This renders the UI Integration Card inside the SAPUI5 application.

 

Step 7: Run the Application

Open the terminal and execute the following command:

npm start

Once the application starts successfully, open:

http://localhost:8080

The application displays the List Card populated with data from the local JSON file.

Output:

 

Step 8: Test the Master-Detail Interaction

Click any record displayed in the List Card.

When a user selects a record:

  • The ShowCard action is triggered.
  • The inline Object Card opens automatically.
  • The selected record's detailed information is displayed.
  • The detail view remains within the same interaction flow, creating a simple Master-Detail experience.

Output:

 

Final Output

Click any item in the List Card to open the Object Card and view the selected record's detailed information.

 

Conclusion

In this blog, we learned how to build interactive SAPUI5 UI Integration Cards using local JSON data. We created a List Card to display summarized information and configured an inline Object Card using the ShowCard action to implement a simple Master-Detail experience.

This approach helps create interactive, reusable, and user-friendly interfaces while keeping the implementation simple within a single card manifest. I hope this blog helps you understand the fundamentals of building List Cards, Object Cards, and implementing Master-Detail navigation using SAPUI5 UI Integration Cards.

 

Thanks and Regards,
Deepa Ramesh Ragho
